news.title: VIP Clothing Limited announced that it expects to receive INR 119.25 million in funding from TRIKAYA CAPITAL PARTNERS PRIVATE LIMITED, SHOKIN PACKAGING PRIVATE LIMITED and other investors
news.body: VIP Clothing Limited announced a private placement of 21,200,000 convertible warrants of the company at a price per warrants of INR 5.625 for gross proceeds of INR 119,250,000 on May 18, 2026. The transaction includes participation from new investors, Trikaya Capital Partners Private Limited for 900,000 warrants, Shokin Packaging Private Limited for 900,000 warrants and from individual investors Sunil Jaykumar Pathare for 4,500,000 warrants, Kapil Jaykumar Pathare for 4,500,000 warrants and other individual investors. The warrant exercise price will be of INR 16.875 and will be exercisable within a maximum period of 18 months from the date of allotment of  warrants. news.title: New minor risk - Share price stability
news.body: The company's share price has been volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 75% of Indian stocks, typically moving 7.4% a week. This is considered a minor risk. Share price volatility indicates the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent. It also increases the risk of potential losses in the short term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Minor Risks Share price has been volatile over the past 3 months (7.4% average weekly change). Market cap is less than US$100m (₹1.83b market cap, or US$20.1m).

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹0.10 (vs ₹0.22 in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.10 (down from ₹0.22 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹512.9m (down 18% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹9.27m (down 54% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 1.8% (down from 3.2% in 3Q 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by lower revenue. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 1% per year but the company’s share price has fallen by 18% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings.
